title: How Amazon Marketplace evaluates content quality with Amazon SageMaker AI
author: James Kim
contentSnippet: A+ Content is the rich media widget on the Amazon product detail page. Through visual assets, brands communicate unique product and brand value to help customers make informed purchase decisions. Selling partners using high-quality A+ Content boost their sales by 8–20 percent compared to those without it. A wide variety of brands, from established brands with large in-house design teams to bootstrapped brands with limited resources, use A+ Content, creating inconsistency in content quality. A typical A+ Content project combines text, images, and video into a cohesive product story. Evaluating each asset in isolation misses the quality that emerges from how those assets work together. When your content spans multiple heterogeneous modules and you need a holistic quality signal rather than per-asset checks, the multi-model fusion approach described in this post can help. In this post, we examine this problem in the context of A+ Content. A+ Content provides creative freedom for selling partners to express their authentic selves on their product detail pages, without strict content specifications such as image ratio and text word count. Although this flexibility allows compelling brand storytelling, it also creates substantial variation in content composition and quality. With quality evaluation and improvement recommendations, brands can transform average content into high-quality content that is more coherent, relevant, and useful. This improved content helps customers make more informed purchasing decisions and build lasting relationships with brands, leading to improved revenue for selling partners. To achieve this goal, an evaluation system must assess the complete content experience, provide actionable recommendations beyond numeric scores, and reflect the nuances across product categories. Existing approaches struggle to meet all these requirements simultaneously, so in this post, you will see a new approach using Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to understand and evaluate content holistically, and a diffusion-based generation component that produces improved visual assets from the resulting quality signals. In this post, you will learn how to: Render complete ecommerce content as a single snapshot and evaluate it holistically with a VLM. Combine VLM semantic scores with OCR readability signals in a lightweight CatBoost classifier trained on expert annotati

summary.tldr:
Amazon has developed a multi-model fusion system using Amazon SageMaker to evaluate the quality of 'A+ Content'—the rich media widgets on product detail pages—which can increase seller sales by 8–20%. Because A+ Content allows brands significant creative freedom without strict constraints on image ratios or word counts, the resulting heterogeneity makes traditional per-asset quality checks ineffective. The system aims to provide a holistic quality signal that accounts for the interaction between text, images, and video rather than evaluating individual components in isolation.

The technical architecture utilizes Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to analyze complete ecommerce content rendered as a single snapshot. This VLM-based evaluation is combined with OCR-derived readability signals and fed into a lightweight CatBoost classifier. The classifier is trained on expert annotations to provide actionable quality feedback. Furthermore, the system integrates a diffusion-based generation component that leverages the quality signals to produce improved visual assets, helping brands refine their content for better coherence and relevance across diverse product categories.
takeaways: **Sales Impact:** Selling partners utilizing high-quality A+ Content report sales increases ranging from 8% to 20%.
**Evaluation Methodology:** The system employs a multi-model fusion approach, rendering full content as a single snapshot for holistic VLM analysis.
**Classifier Architecture:** A lightweight CatBoost classifier is used to synthesize VLM semantic scores and OCR readability signals.
**Generative Component:** The pipeline includes a diffusion-based model designed to generate improved visual assets based on identified quality gaps.

title: OpenAI president Greg Brockman says company could be IPO ready in 2027
author: Sarah Perez
contentSnippet:
OpenAI co-founder and president Greg Brockman said the company would be ready for an IPO in 2027, noting that its enterprise revenue has been growing. Speaking at a Wall Street Journal tech conference on Wednesday, the executive touted how the company had been gaining ground in the enterprise market, where rival Anthropic had already successfully made inroads.

In response to the interviewer’s question about being IPO-ready next year, Brockman replied, “I think so. Yes.”

“We’ve been very clear this year that we want to go public when we feel is the right time for us, and I feel extremely good about the business. I feel like we’ve made so much progress this year, and I’ve honestly never felt more confident in what we’re doing,” Brockman said.

He detailed how OpenAI’s trajectory as an enterprise had changed over the course of 2026, noting that the first and second quarters were “pretty rough.” He also admitted that OpenAI “wasn’t even in the conversation” when it came to agentic coding — an area where Anthropic’s Claude Code has gained market share.

“We had Codex, but no one was talking about it,” Brockman continued, “and I think that we just kept our heads down and executed.”

By the third quarter, activity picked up, as OpenAI saw 70% quarterly growth in its annualized revenue — something Brockman attributed to the enterprise side of the business doubling. He explained that the growth wasn’t simply the result of something that happened in the quarter itself, but rather the culmination of investments the company had been making up to that point.

Now the majority of OpenAI’s revenue is coming from the enterprise business, which previously accounted for only around 30% of its total revenue.

“And it’s not that consumer [revenue has shrunk] … It’s been growing, but it’s the enterprise segment has really taken off,” he said, pointing to a recent partnership with JPMorgan Chase as one example of the type of client it’s now winning deals with.

Brockman also spoke more broadly about the lessons OpenAI learned from selling into the enterprise market as well. He said the company had come to understand that its job was to help businesses identify the most important milestones they could achieve with its AI technology, build trust with clients, and demonstrate that it was a reliable partner for the long haul.

“A year ago, we weren’t even really in the enterprise g

summary.tldr:
OpenAI co-founder and president Greg Brockman stated that the company could be ready for an initial public offering (IPO) by 2027. Speaking at a Wall Street Journal tech conference, Brockman expressed high confidence in the company's current business trajectory, noting that 2026 began with "rough" performance in the first and second quarters before accelerating significantly in the third quarter.

OpenAI reported a 70% quarterly growth in annualized revenue during Q3 2026, a surge driven primarily by the enterprise segment. Enterprise revenue now accounts for the majority of the company's total income, a shift from its previous status where enterprise deals represented only 30% of the total. Brockman highlighted a partnership with JPMorgan Chase as a key indicator of the company's successful pivot from a consumer-focused brand to a reliable enterprise partner, specifically noting that the company had previously struggled to compete in the agentic coding space against Anthropic’s Claude Code.
takeaways: **IPO Timeline:** Greg Brockman confirmed that OpenAI could be ready for an IPO by 2027.
**Revenue Growth:** The company achieved 70% quarterly growth in annualized revenue during Q3 2026.
**Enterprise Shift:** Enterprise business has grown to represent the majority of total revenue, up from approximately 30% previously.
**Competitive Context:** OpenAI acknowledged losing early market share in agentic coding to Anthropic’s Claude Code during the first half of 2026.
**Key Client:** JPMorgan Chase was cited as a primary example of the enterprise-level clients OpenAI is currently securing.

title: Claude can now analyze your spending with its new Personal Finance tool
author: Aisha Malik
contentSnippet:
Anthropic announced Thursday that Claude is getting a new tool called “Personal Finance,” designed to help users keep track of their money. With it, users can connect their bank and credit card accounts through Plaid and ask Claude questions about their finances. Anthropic says access is read-only, meaning Personal Finance can’t move, manage, or invest users’ money.

By letting Claude connect directly to bank and credit card accounts, Anthropic is positioning its chatbot as a financial companion that can help people understand their spending and make sense of their money, rather than simply offering them generic advice.

With the launch, Claude is playing catch-up to OpenAI’s ChatGPT, which introduced similar personal finance tools in May that also let users connect their financial accounts and ask questions about everything from spending patterns to long-term financial planning.

“Claude gives you answers in everyday language, from your balances and transactions, and explains any term that’s new to you,” Anthropic wrote in a blog post. “Like the rest of Claude, Personal Finance has no ads or sponsored recommendations, and it doesn’t offer credit cards, loans, or savings accounts of its own, so your money questions get a straight answer.”

For instance, at the end of the month, a user could ask Claude, “Where did my money go this month?” The chatbot will then add up spending across the connected accounts and sort it by category, such as rent and utilities, food and drink, and shopping. Users can choose to go deeper by following up with questions like, “Is that more than usual?” or “Anything else I’m missing?”

Anthropic says the tool goes beyond basic spending summaries by analyzing transactions across connected accounts to flag potential issues, such as duplicate charges, unexpected fees, and steadily increasing bills. Users can also ask broader questions about their finances, such as whether they’re spending more than they earn. The tool can also explain financial concepts like APR (annual percentage rate), while providing calculations that show users how much they’ve paid in interest over the past year.

Of course, some people will have reservations about connecting their financial accounts to an AI chatbot. Anthropic says Claude’s access is limited to each connected bank’s name, account name and type, the last four digits of the account number, balances,

summary.tldr:
Anthropic has introduced a "Personal Finance" tool for Claude, enabling users to connect bank and credit card accounts via Plaid to receive AI-driven insights into their spending habits. The feature provides read-only access to financial data, preventing the model from executing transactions, moving funds, or managing investments. Anthropic explicitly states that conversations within the Personal Finance hub are excluded from model training, and the service contains no advertisements or sponsored financial product recommendations.

The tool allows users to query their financial data in natural language, offering capabilities such as categorizing monthly expenditures, identifying duplicate charges, flagging unexpected fees, and tracking rising bills. Beyond transaction summaries, Claude can explain financial terminology like APR and calculate interest payments over the past year. The system accesses specific data points including account names, types, balances, credit limits, the last four digits of account numbers, and up to two years of transaction history. This launch positions Claude as a direct competitor to OpenAI’s ChatGPT, which integrated similar financial account connectivity in May.

Personal Finance is currently rolling out in beta for U.S.-based users subscribed to Pro, Max, and Ultra plans. This release follows Anthropic’s broader strategy to target specific professional verticals, building on the earlier launches of "Claude for Legal" and "Claude for Financial Services."
takeaways: **Data Access Scope:** Claude is limited to reading account names, types, balances, credit limits, last four digits of account numbers, and up to 24 months of transaction history.

**Privacy Protections:** Conversations within the Personal Finance hub are explicitly excluded from model training, and the tool operates on a read-only basis with no capability to execute financial transactions.
**Availability:** The beta rollout is restricted to U.S. users on Pro, Max, and Ultra subscription tiers.
**Technical Integration:** The tool utilizes Plaid to facilitate secure connections to external financial institutions.
**Functional Capabilities:** The model can perform automated categorization of expenses, detect duplicate charges, calculate annual interest payments, and explain complex financial concepts like APR.

title: Claude AI can plug directly into your bank account
author: Jess Weatherbed
contentSnippet: Anthropic has a new pitch for managing your personal finances: let Claude do it instead, with a new Personal Finance feature that connects it to your bank and card accounts via the Plaid bank bridging platform. You can ask the chatbot “where did my money go this month,” for example, and it’ll create an overview with a breakdown of spending by category, including rent and utilities, shopping, and food. Claude can also answer broader questions around what bills are left before your next payday, if you can afford big purchases like holiday trips, and how much money you could be saving each month. Its access is read-only, and with Plaid facilitating the connection, Claude doesn’t see your banking passwords and your bank doesn’t have to deal with unvetted AI bots crawling around your accounts. Claude can’t move, manage, or invest your money, according to Anthropic, and it “isn’t designed to give investment advice.”, but it can see the bank’s name, account names, account type, the last four digits of the number associated with it, your balances and credit limits, and up to two years’ worth of your transaction history. [Media: https://youtu.be/UTubvRLX2j4?is=83QNW4I8cQha8f0d ] If you choose to give it access to all that, Claude can explain financial terms you don’t understand and answer questions about your balances and transactions. Personal Finance in Claude is rolling out in beta this week to Claude Pro, Max, and Ultra plan subscribers in the US. Anthropic’s announcement follows OpenAI introducing a similar feature for ChatGPT in May, which also plugs into your bank accounts through Plaid. Allowing AI to have oversight into your finances might ring some alarm bells, but according to the sign-off in Anthropic’s press release, it’s just the beginning: > “Personal Finance is a first step. For life’s bigger money decisions, we think people are best served by Claude working alongside the licensed professionals and regulated firms they trust. We’re exploring how to make that possible in Claude, and we’d like to hear from banks, wealth managers, and financial services companies who want to help shape it.”

summary.tldr:
Anthropic has launched a 'Personal Finance' feature for its Claude AI assistant, enabling users to connect their bank and credit card accounts via the Plaid API. The integration allows Claude to analyze up to two years of transaction history to provide spending breakdowns by category, identify upcoming bills, and assess affordability for large purchases. The feature is currently rolling out in beta to Claude Pro, Max, and Ultra subscribers in the United States.

Technically, the integration is read-only, meaning Claude cannot initiate transfers, manage investments, or execute financial transactions. Through the Plaid bridge, the model gains access to specific metadata including bank names, account types, the last four digits of account numbers, current balances, and credit limits. Anthropic explicitly states the tool is not designed to provide investment advice. This rollout mirrors a similar integration introduced by OpenAI for ChatGPT in May 2024.

Anthropic frames this as an initial step toward broader financial integration. The company is actively soliciting partnerships with banks, wealth managers, and regulated financial institutions to explore future capabilities where Claude might work alongside licensed professionals for more complex financial decision-making.
takeaways: **Integration Architecture:** Uses Plaid as a third-party intermediary to facilitate read-only access to banking data without exposing user passwords to Anthropic.
**Data Scope:** Claude can access up to two years of transaction history, account balances, credit limits, and account metadata.
**Availability:** Currently limited to US-based Claude Pro, Max, and Ultra plan subscribers.
**Functional Constraints:** The system is restricted from moving, managing, or investing funds and is not authorized to provide formal investment advice.
**Strategic Roadmap:** Anthropic is seeking collaboration with regulated financial firms to expand the tool's utility for high-level financial planning.

title: Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout
author: Tushaar Gangavarapu, Gil Tabak, Clemens JS Schaefer
contentSnippet: Linear attention compresses context into a fixed-size key-value state for linear-time training and constant-memory inference. Gated delta-rule models decay this state and erase its prediction for an incoming key before writing a new value; Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) generalizes this with channel-wise decay and decoupled, full-rank erase and write gates. However, we show that state updates are far less sensitive to erasure than to writes: key activation and unit normalization concentrate key energy onto a sparse subset of channels, whereas value writes scale all channels, so the erase gate can be parameterized at lower rank. Furthermore, slow-decaying state rows accumulate much larger norms than fast rows, dominating unweighted readout and forcing stronger write-time erasure to suppress interference. Guided by this analysis, we introduce Muir, which fuses all gates into a sensitivity-allocated low-rank projection, re-weights state rows with a matched-filter readout gate, and reinvests the saved parameters in a wider feed-forward network. Because standard chunkwise algorithms become numerically unstable at the large chunk sizes needed to saturate wide matrix units, we design a parallel update for stable, efficient training. Across 166M-1.34B parameters, Muir lowers perplexity by 1.8-2.0% over GDN-2 and 2.5-3.6% over Transformer, raises commonsense accuracy by up to 1.9 points, and improves extractive recall over GDN-2. At 1.34B, Muir outperforms both baselines on multi-hop and multi-needle recall, extrapolates 2,560x from its 4K training length to 10M-token streams without perplexity drift, and maintains near-100% passkey retrieval to 1M tokens with static readout. Muir achieves these gains while matching GDN-2 throughput, reaching its 100B-token validation loss 1.2x faster, and training 2.7x faster than Transformer at 32K.

summary.tldr:
Muir is a new linear attention architecture that improves upon Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) by optimizing state update sensitivity and readout mechanisms. By analyzing the disparity between erase and write gate sensitivity—where key activation concentrates energy on sparse channels while value writes affect all channels—the researchers implemented a sensitivity-allocated low-rank projection. This design allows for the parameter-efficient fusion of gates, enabling the reinvestment of saved parameters into wider feed-forward networks. To address numerical instability in standard chunkwise algorithms, the authors developed a parallel update method that facilitates stable training at the large chunk sizes required to saturate modern matrix hardware.

In empirical evaluations across models ranging from 166M to 1.34B parameters, Muir demonstrated a 1.8-2.0% perplexity reduction over GDN-2 and a 2.5-3.6% improvement over standard Transformers. The model shows significant gains in extractive recall and commonsense reasoning, with the 1.34B variant achieving superior multi-hop and multi-needle recall. Notably, Muir exhibits robust long-context capabilities, extrapolating 2,560x from a 4K training length to 10M-token streams without perplexity drift, while maintaining near-100% passkey retrieval up to 1M tokens using static readout. The architecture achieves these performance gains while matching GDN-2 throughput, reaching 100B-token validation loss 1.2x faster and training 2.7x faster than Transformers at a 32K context window.
takeaways: **Architecture Optimization:** Muir fuses erase and write gates into a sensitivity-allocated low-rank projection, re-weighting state rows via a matched-filter readout gate.
**Performance Benchmarks:** Muir achieves 1.8-2.0% lower perplexity than GDN-2 and 2.5-3.6% lower than Transformers, with up to 1.9 points higher commonsense accuracy.
**Long-Context Scaling:** The model supports 2,560x length extrapolation (4K to 10M tokens) and maintains near-100% passkey retrieval accuracy up to 1M tokens.
**Training Efficiency:** Muir reaches 100B-token validation loss 1.2x faster than GDN-2 and trains 2.7x faster than Transformer baselines at 32K context.
**Numerical Stability:** The authors introduced a custom parallel update algorithm to enable stable training at large chunk sizes, overcoming limitations in standard chunkwise implementations.

title: ‘Total repudiation’: The blue wave is about to hit AI
author: Hayden Field
contentSnippet: On Tuesday night, Democrats made history as they took control of the House and the Senate, and a blue wave swept through traditionally red and swing states — with the nation’s first Black woman governor elected in Georgia, the country’s first Native American woman governor elected in New Mexico, and a Maine Senator ceding to a Democrat after 30 years in office. In these and other campaigns, one theme kept coming up: holding AI companies accountable to the American people. Now, the AI industry is left considering the prospect of regulation, data center construction slowdowns, and more. Publicly, most major AI company CEOs have remained silent. OpenAI and Anthropic did not provide comments to The Verge; Elon Musk’s call on X to vote “red” for the midterms — the SpaceX CEO had spent close to $450 million backing Republican campaigns for the election — vanished after results poured in. Privately, CEOs have discussed significant compute capacity constraints for their companies after Tuesday’s results, particularly OpenAI, per The Wall Street Journal. Meta’s platforms president, Dina Powell McCormick, says many are considering moving data center construction abroad. AI executives are reportedly privately nervous about the results but may also be able to blame them for not delivering as much revenue to investors. Many of the incoming leaders have promised to drag CEOs to testify. On X, a popular post by former X product lead Nikita Bier warned that “This is going to be like the Nuremberg Trials but for AI researchers.” (On Tuesday night, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman did post about how “people should always be in control of the future,” but he spent other parts of the evening talking about RAM.) Tuesday’s results were a “total repudiation” of the AI field, says Wes McEnany, the former Deputy Labor Policy Director of the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, & Pensions, who now works with the nonprofit Future of Life Institute. He said that AI touches “every aspect of people’s lives,” whether they’re applying for jobs, using social media, or even paying electricity bills while living near a data center, and that they’re tired of not having “any agency in that conversation.” The bipartisan backlash against data center construction is the most tangible manifestation of that backlash. It’s going to be unquestionably more difficult to build them across the country, afte

summary.tldr:
Following recent midterm election results, the AI industry faces a significant shift in political landscape as Democrats secured control of both the House and Senate. The election cycle featured widespread voter concern regarding AI accountability, with local data center construction emerging as a primary point of contention. Industry analysts and observers, including those from the Future of Life Institute and The Tech Oversight Project, characterize the results as a "total repudiation" of current AI expansion strategies, noting that 43 out of 44 local ballot measures aimed at restricting data center construction were passed by voters.

Privately, AI executives are reportedly bracing for increased compute capacity constraints and potential regulatory hurdles. Meta’s platforms president, Dina Powell McCormick, indicated that companies are considering relocating data center construction abroad to circumvent domestic opposition. While some industry figures suggest the slowdown could prevent an AI market bubble, others anticipate a wave of "tech accountability" legislation. Incoming leadership has signaled intentions to mandate congressional testimony for AI CEOs, and experts suggest that previous federal efforts to preempt state-level AI restrictions are now effectively dead, leaving companies vulnerable to a patchwork of stringent local and state-level regulations.
takeaways: **Data Center Moratoria:** 43 out of 44 local ballot measures aimed at restricting data center construction were approved by voters.
**Public Sentiment:** An NBC News poll indicated that 76 percent of voters oppose the construction of data centers within their local communities.
**Legislative Outlook:** Experts, including those from the Guardrails Alliance, suggest that federal attempts to bar state-level AI restrictions are now "completely dead."
**Proposed Legislation:** Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Greg Casar introduced a bill in September aimed at banning "superintelligence."
**Industry Response:** Analysts at Yorkville Ives & Co. project that the current political climate could delay the construction of up to 1,000 planned data centers across the U.S.

title: University of Utah retains operational sovereignty as Redtail expands research access
author: Victoria Gayton
contentSnippet:
UPDATED 12:35 EST / NOVEMBER 05 2026

University of Utah retains operational sovereignty as Redtail expands research access

Operational sovereignty gives universities authority over how shared computing resources are allocated, managed and secured.

The University of Utah’s Redtail AI factory supercomputer brings advanced computing capabilities to a statewide community. Supporting researchers, students, administrators and external partners through that infrastructure requires more than computing capacity, according to Manish Parashar (pictured), chief AI officer of the University of Utah.

“In research, we are always trying to balance research security with doing open research for societal good,” he said. “Depending on where you are, you might want to lean in one direction or the other. Having that capability to turn the knob becomes so important.”

Parashar spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante and Amit Eyal Govrin for the “Sovereign AI: From Strategy to Reality” video series , during an exclusive interview on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed university control of computing infrastructure, research governance and the investment needed to support Utah’s expanding ambitions. (* Disclosure below.)

Operational sovereignty starts with university expertise

Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. helped architect and deploy Redtail as a turnkey system. The university’s Center for High Performance Computing operates it, drawing on expertise that also supports separate regulated research environments, Parashar explained.

“They have admin access, they’re doing the allocations, they are doing the onboarding,” he said. “They’re doing the management and monitoring … the optimization [and] … the right sizing.”

The interview examined Utah’s approach through theCUBE Research’s Five Pillars of Sovereign AI framework : Territorial, Legal, Technological, Operational and Financial. The university retains operational and legal responsibilities, while financing rests on partnerships with the state and donors, according to Parashar.

“Our overall ecosystem is a hybrid,” he said. “There’s things that are on-prem, there are things that are cloud-hosted, and we always will look at it as a hybrid system. Not everything has to be territorially in a single data center or in the state.”

summary.tldr:
The University of Utah has implemented a "Redtail" AI factory supercomputer, architected and deployed by Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) as a turnkey system. Managed by the university's Center for High Performance Computing, the infrastructure is designed to provide "operational sovereignty," allowing the institution to maintain direct control over resource allocation, security, and management. This approach enables the university to balance open research initiatives with the requirements of sensitive, regulated projects, such as healthcare data, by migrating open research workloads to Redtail and freeing up capacity in existing, highly-regulated data centers.

Under the "One-U Responsible AI" initiative, the university is leveraging this hybrid infrastructure—which spans on-premises and cloud-hosted environments—to address regional challenges like air quality. The university is currently pursuing a multi-pronged financial strategy to ensure the sustainability of the ecosystem, engaging with the state government, philanthropic donors, and federal agencies including the Department of Energy and the National Science Foundation. The project is framed within theCUBE Research’s "Five Pillars of Sovereign AI" (Territorial, Legal, Technological, Operational, and Financial), with the university retaining legal and operational responsibility while utilizing external partnerships for financing and technical deployment.
takeaways: **Infrastructure Partner:** Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) served as the architect and deployment partner for the Redtail AI factory supercomputer.
**Operational Model:** The University of Utah utilizes a hybrid infrastructure strategy, combining on-premises resources with cloud-hosted environments to maintain operational sovereignty.

**Strategic Goal:** The deployment of Redtail is intended to offload open research workloads, thereby increasing available capacity in existing data centers for sensitive, regulated research projects.

**Funding Strategy:** The university is actively seeking capital from the state, philanthropic donors, and federal entities like the Department of Energy and the National Science Foundation to support technology refreshes and expansion.

**Governance Framework:** The project is aligned with theCUBE Research’s "Five Pillars of Sovereign AI," which categorizes the initiative across territorial, legal, technological, operational, and financial dimensions.

Google DeepMind has released Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, an updated video generation model featuring native 15-second clip generation, improved reference adherence, and multi-turn conversational editing. The model is now generally available across the Gemini API, Google Cloud, Google Vids, and Google Ads. title: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents
author: NVIDIA Writers
contentSnippet: Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs. Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities. Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem.   Create Editable 3D Assets With Houdini and AI Agents Creating animated 3D content requires connecting modeling, simulation, materials and rendering. Nick Scarcella, a senior technical artist on NVIDIA’s BondLab team, directed AI agents — primarily using Claude — to work with CUDA libraries and Isaac Sim to create animations. The BondLab team uses SideFX Houdini and the NVIDIA ovrtx library to develop materials, lighting and the final rendered appearance. In one experiment, Scarcella guided Astra to recreate an OP-1 portable synthesizer using product images, manuals and technical direction. He exported the model into the OpenUSD framework, tested it in Houdini and Blender, then used Astra and Opus to refine details before adjusting materials and textures for ovrtx rendering. Scarcella also used a publicly shared robot-hand checkpoint in Isaac Sim, directing the motion and developing materials and lighting in Houdini with Claude’s assistance. Working with team member Steven Dvornik, the team created an “Echos” visualization: translucent versions of the hand overlap and merge into a single hand animation, offering a visual interpretation of robot training. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Robot_Hand_Video_Omniverse.mp4 Figure: An artistic visualization of simulated robot-hand motion, developed with AI assistance and Houdini’s materials and lighting tools. These workflows bring agent-assisted creation into existing artist tools, giving teams editable content they can inspect, refine and render across applications. summary.tldr:
NVIDIA’s BondLab team is integrating frontier AI agents, including Claude and Astra, with the NVIDIA Omniverse platform to automate the creation of 3D assets and simulations. By leveraging natural-language instructions, developers can interface with GPU-accelerated libraries like Isaac Sim, CUDA, and ovrtx to manage complex workflows involving modeling, physics, and rendering. The process utilizes the OpenUSD framework to ensure interoperability between tools such as SideFX Houdini, Blender, and Omniverse, allowing for the iterative refinement of 3D content.

In a practical application, senior technical artist Nick Scarcella demonstrated this workflow by recreating an OP-1 portable synthesizer using product documentation and images, subsequently refining the model through AI-assisted texture and material adjustments. The team also utilized a robot-hand checkpoint in Isaac Sim to develop an 'Echos' visualization, which uses translucent, overlapping layers to represent robot training data. These agent-driven workflows are designed to produce fully editable 3D assets that can be inspected and rendered across multiple industry-standard applications.
takeaways: **Tooling Integration:** The workflow connects AI agents with SideFX Houdini, Blender, and NVIDIA’s ovrtx library for material, lighting, and rendering tasks.
**Framework Standards:** All assets are exported into the OpenUSD framework to maintain compatibility across different 3D software environments.
**Agent Utilization:** NVIDIA’s BondLab team primarily employs Claude and Astra to execute tasks within CUDA libraries and Isaac Sim via natural-language prompting.
**Visualization Technique:** The 'Echos' project visualizes robot training by layering translucent versions of a robot hand to show motion paths and merging sequences.

title: Grimes is going to star in an AI movie that’s coming to theaters
author: Andrew Webster
contentSnippet: The AI-generated sci-fi film Gods Don’t Give Gifts has added a bit of star power: Pop star Grimes is going to appear in the movie. Billed as “the first AI film to come to theatres,” Gods Don’t Give Gifts is a notable test case for the commercial potential of AI films, and it releases on December 4th. Grimes — who will be lending both her likeness and vocal performance to the movie, which you can see in the clip above — potentially gives the project some legitimacy. AI studio Fable, which is producing the film, claimed in a press release that “casting the likeness of an actor with their spoken vocal performance will become more common with animated films using AI: audiences will see actors, athletes, musicians giving vocal performances with their likeness in films.” Gods Don’t Give Gifts is being directed by Jack London, better known under the online handle Gossip Goblin. Gods Don’t Give Gifts is an anthology that’s set in a future “where bodies are disposable and consciousness has been commoditized” and depicts what happens when “four interconnected stories collide with the horrifying consequences of humanity’s attempt to transcend the flesh.” Those themes seem to fit pretty snugly with Grimes’ interests, as she has explored themes of transhumanism and artificial intelligence in the past. It’s also not the only AI project she’s working on, with an AI-themed album called Psy Opera in the works. Here’s the trailer for Gods Don’t Give Gifts: [Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1G5LArU7tmE] While there has been plenty of hype around the potential for AI in Hollywood, there’s yet to be a project that shows that the technology is actually a vital storytelling tool. Previous examples, like two different takes on The Odyssey — including one made with Elon Musk’s Grok — have left plenty to be desired.

summary.tldr:
Pop artist Grimes has joined the cast of 'Gods Don’t Give Gifts,' an anthology sci-fi film produced by AI studio Fable that is marketed as the first AI-generated feature to receive a theatrical release. Scheduled for a December 4th premiere, the project utilizes AI to synthesize both Grimes' likeness and vocal performance, a production model Fable posits will become standard for future animated and AI-driven cinema. The film explores themes of transhumanism, specifically a future where consciousness is commoditized and physical bodies are considered disposable.

The film is directed by Jack London, known online as 'Gossip Goblin.' The narrative structure consists of four interconnected stories centered on the consequences of humanity attempting to transcend biological limitations. This project aligns with Grimes' established creative focus on AI and transhumanist aesthetics, as she is simultaneously developing an AI-themed album titled 'Psy Opera.' The release serves as a commercial test case for AI-generated storytelling in Hollywood, following previous, less critically successful attempts at AI-assisted film production, such as adaptations of 'The Odyssey' involving Elon Musk’s Grok.
takeaways: **Release Date:** The film is scheduled to hit theaters on December 4th.
**Production Studio:** The project is produced by Fable, an AI-focused studio.
**Director:** The film is directed by Jack London, who operates under the handle 'Gossip Goblin.'
**Technical Scope:** The film features AI-synthesized likeness and vocal performances, with a narrative focused on the commoditization of consciousness.
